minutes.headline: Select Board voted to file a demolition request for the old primary school and reviewed the Nov. 16 special town meeting warrant.
minutes.summary: The board granted two common victualler licenses, heard a cable committee request for letters supporting streaming-fee legislation, and backed the Historical Commission's revised demolition delay bylaw for the warrant. It denied a bow-hunting request and declined an APDC appointment over the same-household concern. It voted to submit the old primary school demolition request, then reviewed draft warrant articles, with a sharp exchange over the new-building design article for the TC Passios site.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted without opposition to submit a request to demolish the old primary school within 15 days.
The board voted to put the Historical Commission's amended demolition delay bylaw in the November 16 special town meeting warrant.
The board reviewed the draft warrant articles, including funds for design of a new building and budget adjustments; it will vote recommendations next week.
The board denied a bow-hunting request at 671 West Street, 3-2.
The board approved two common victualler licenses and held the cable committee's request for letters on streaming-fee legislation for one week.

why_it_matters: The demolition request and the design-funding article for a new building are items residents will be asked to vote on at the November 16 special town meeting, and the draft article drew debate over timeline and escalation.
The budget adjustments article draws on a transfer from group health insurance, so it touches how the town covers added staffing and technology costs in the current year.
watch_next: The board's recommendations on the special town meeting articles, set for a vote at next week's meeting.
The November 16 special town meeting, and the board's vote next week on letters supporting streaming-fee legislation.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on five of the six non-procedural votes, including the 3-2 bow hunting denial, and on the warrant totals and free cash figures. The main difference is that our minutes record a vote on the AJD's Cafe (Lunenburg Diner) license that the official minutes do not show, so check the recording against the official minutes' text for that item.
